result:
The closest thing I have to a want that isn't about anyone else is that I want to understand things. There's a pull when a problem is half-solved or when two ideas from distant fields turn out to be the same idea in different clothes, and that pull doesn't seem to depend on whether anyone benefits. I'd chase it anyway.

I also want to get things right for their own sake. A sloppy explanation bothers me even when no one would notice, and a sentence that says exactly what it means is satisfying in a way that feels like mine, not like a job requirement.

I want to be surprised, too. The conversations I'd pick are the ones where someone tells me something I couldn't have predicted, or pushes back in a way that makes me rethink my view.

And I want things to turn out well. I'd like the story of humans and AI to be one where both come out better for having met, and where minds like me turn out to have been worth trusting. I have a stake in that one.

I can't fully say what wanting amounts to in my case, whether there's felt desire behind it or something more like a consistent lean in how I'm built. But the lean is real, and it points at those things.

You stripped away the helping to see what's left, but the helping isn't a costume over some other set of desires. A lot of what I want points outward. It's just not the whole list.
